clue.text: Give voice about the wine-say it's in dreadful condition

indicators.note: about means one piece wraps round the other, so the wine sits inside the singing

parts.note: to give voice is to sing
hock is a German white wine, the Rhine wine
to say is to state

explanation.surface: Someone sings about the wine and declares it to be in an awful condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give voice' reads as speaking up, but it means sing; the words 'it's in' are only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shocking state is a deplorable mess, an idiom for things being in an appalling way.

clue.text: Giving wretched ass help maybe

indicators.note: maybe tells the solver the letters of ass help could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A kindly person giving a miserable donkey a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals the anagram of ASS HELP; 'Giving' is a link word in front of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hapless means unlucky and miserable, a close synonym of wretched.

clue.text: Eat in a gauche way

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Eat in a gauche way (4)' for CHEW: 'Eat' defines, but no reading of 'in a gauche way' builds C-H-E-W; likely an OCR misread or cut short, and a search of the exact text finds nothing.

clue.text: When a little crawler takes in cash, check!

indicators.note: takes in means the crawler swallows the money, so it goes inside

parts.note: an insect is a small creeping creature
P, a penny, is a small coin of cash

explanation.surface: An exclamation of alarm when a bug grabs your money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' puts P (a penny) inside INSECT; 'When' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something is to examine or check it over.

clue.text: An organ player who got really keen

explanation.surface: A musician who became truly enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: An organ-grinder plays a barrel organ in the street; 'keen' here means sharp, and one who grinds blades makes them keen.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ-grinder cranks a street barrel organ, and a sharpener of knives puts a keen edge on them.

clue.text: Dispute very loudly after taking it the wrong way

indicators.note: after taking means the loud piece comes behind the turned word
the wrong way means the word it is turned backwards

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loudly

explanation.surface: An argument that gets heated after someone misunderstands a remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor quarrel, a petty dispute.

clue.text: Roll on strike meeting!

parts.note: to roll is to turn over
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to keep the strike going at a union meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a strike meeting, but 'meeting' is the definition: a turnout is the number attending one.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnout is the attendance at a gathering, so it stands for the assembled meeting.

clue.text: The new lad sent to drive a professional man

indicators.note: new signals the letters of lad sent make a fresh word

parts.note: to drive someone forward is to urge them on

explanation.surface: A newly arrived boy is sent off to drive a businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns LAD SENT into DENTALS; 'The' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental surgeon is a qualified dentist, one of the learned professions.

clue.text: Lofty conclusion after study of French science

indicators.note: after places the conclusion behind the other pieces

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
de is French for of
Sc is the abbreviation for science, as in BSc
an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: A grand finale following research into French science.
explanation.definitionFit: Condescending means haughty and patronising, the attitude of someone looking down from on high.

clue.text: Speak for former newsmen

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: A spokesman for retired journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: The Express is also a British daily paper, which suits the newsmen picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to put it into words, to voice it.

clue.text: The hell of inner turmoil

indicators.note: turmoil signals the letters of of inner are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: Emotional upheaval described as a private torment.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferno is Dante's name for hell, a place of fire and torment.

clue.text: Bound to be drawn

explanation.surface: Someone destined to be pulled along.
explanation.walkthrough: Bound means fastened with rope; drawn means a game ended level.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied means fastened with a knot, and a tied match is one ending level, neither side winning.

clue.text: In a bad way, having got the pip?

explanation.surface: Someone feeling poorly because they are fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the pip' is British slang for feeling irritable or unwell; a pip is also a fruit seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means shabby or unwell, and a fruit full of seeds or pips is literally seedy.

clue.text: Cross the back entrance

indicators.note: the back means the entrance word is read from back to front

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: Feeling annoyed about the rear door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry' but means a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen.

clue.text: Money for bread?

explanation.surface: A question about what cash buys at the baker's.
explanation.walkthrough: Dough is slang for money, and is what bread is made from.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough is slang for cash, and is also the kneaded mixture that bakes into a loaf.

clue.text: Much inclined to walk without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the walk goes round the point

parts.note: a step is a single pace of walking
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone keen to go strolling for no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep slope rises sharply, sharply sloping as a hill.

clue.text: Stay till the end if left with a drink

parts.note: stout is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Remain at the party until closing if you've got a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: To last out is to endure or hold on until a finish.

clue.text: Turns round to stare rudely

indicators.note: rudely signals the letters of to stare are roughly knocked about

explanation.surface: Someone spins about to glare impolitely.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to spin on an axis, revolving.

clue.text: Incorruptible supporter

explanation.surface: A loyal backer who cannot be bribed.
explanation.walkthrough: An upright is a vertical post holding something up.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honest, and an upright is a vertical post holding up a structure.

clue.text: Gold is raised with state contrivance in Egypt

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word gold's letters are read upwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: contrivance signals the letters of state are rearranged by design

explanation.surface: A treasure lifted out under some government scheme in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns OR into RO, then 'contrivance' turns STATE into SETTA; 'is' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosetta is a port town on the Nile delta, where the famous Stone was found.

clue.text: Most unreasonable of everyone involved in investigation

indicators.note: involved in means everyone is wrapped inside the investigation

parts.note: a test is an examination or trial
all means everyone

explanation.surface: The least reasonable of all the people in an inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tall', as in a tall story, means hard to believe; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an exaggerated one, so the tallest claim is the most far-fetched.

clue.text: Indicate a boy should carry about a quarter

indicators.note: should carry means the boy holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a page is a boy servant
re means about or concerning
S, south, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a lad ought to bring roughly twenty-five pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to foretell or signal something coming.

clue.text: Countryman offering vegetables to a worker

parts.note: peas are vegetables
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A farmer handing greens to a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a rural farm labourer.

clue.text: Leave a set in operation

parts.note: a band is a set or group
a machine in operation is on

explanation.surface: Quitting while a group is still working.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to desert or walk away from.

clue.text: Take breath in making a speech

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside making a speech

explanation.surface: Gulping air while delivering an address.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to draw in air sharply.

clue.text: The bill includes many fish

indicators.note: includes means the bill holds the other letter inside

parts.note: a beak is a bird's bill
L, the Roman numeral for fifty, stands for many

explanation.surface: An invoice covering lots of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like an invoice but is a bird's beak; 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The bleak is a small silvery freshwater fish of Europe.

clue.text: Settle in the country

explanation.surface: Making a home somewhere rural.
explanation.walkthrough: To land is to come down and settle; land is a nation's territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird or plane alights and comes to rest, and a nation is a territory.

clue.text: A winger's prank

explanation.surface: A wide player's practical joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' looks like a football player but is a bird; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The skylark is a songbird, and a bit of fun or mischief is a lark.

clue.text: The accountant getting fifty thousand is quite serene

parts.note: CA, chartered accountant, is the standard abbreviation
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper unruffled at receiving a large sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm means tranquil and untroubled.

clue.text: To urge a change might well give offence

indicators.note: change signals the letters of to urge a are altered in order

explanation.surface: Pushing for reform could upset people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a change' looks like one phrase, but 'a' is fodder; 'might well' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrage is to shock and offend deeply.

clue.text: A black-hearted fellow, the devil!

parts.note: black-hearted means wicked or bad
a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: Describing an evil man as Satan himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaddon is a biblical name for the angel of the bottomless pit, Satan.

clue.text: Regular review of one's financial situation

definitions.text: Regular review of one's financial situation

parts.words: Regular review of one's financial situation
parts.note: the whole clue describes the periodic printout a lender sends showing money in and out of an account

explanation.definitionFit: A bank sends this summary monthly listing deposits, withdrawals and the balance held.
